reviews.title: Very frustrating
reviews.text: Many times when I go to complete a course it can’t hear or recognize what I’m saying. I’ve adjusted settings several times. Warning for anyone with a softer voice tone. It may not always hear you. I would also like this program more if it would teach you the sounds of the language first as well as the alphabet. When you start seeing letters that’s your not used to it would be nice to have an understanding of how they are pronounced. I use the translator a lot on my phone as I find that easier than trying to go through the app.

reviews.title: No translations. Horrible app
reviews.text: Update! Per developer response that there is a translate icon, I checked but I don’t have it. Per support the translate icon is not available in the app. Still a useless miserable experience. If the translate feature becomes available in the app I would like to use it.  This app uses immersion learning which may be successful if you’re surrounded by people who speak the language you’re trying to learn. It doesn’t provide any translations. The pictures are not clear. It spends way too much time on ridiculously simple sound repetition. And very little time on verb conjugations and pronouns. I already paid for a year so I will continue to use it but I have a translation app open on a separate device to make it functional. It’s absolute terrible way to learn a language. I’ve learned there are much better choices than this app.

reviews.title: I feel as if the app got worse
reviews.text: Rosetta Stone app on mobile already suffered from a couple of minor bugs, less-than-ideal speech recognition, and was poorly optimized for a small screen, and, unfortunately, it appears the app has yet regressed some. Now, the app no longer allows you to tackle its lessons at your own pace. You are forced to move along at breakneck speed without so much as an option to review and study previous mistakes. I had the automatically continue to next screen option turned off and it used to work as intended, but now I'm left without recourse. Now I come to find out there's a new version of Rosetta Stone, that doesn't work with my unlimited subscription, and I'm left to wonder if therein lie the cause of this dip in quality. I feel gypped honestly.

I’m often graded incorrectly simply because I started speaking too early or too late.  The sweet spot seems to be waiting one second after the microphone indicates it is listening.

reviews.title: Very frustrating, voice recognition problem still not fixed
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for years. And for years, there have been issues with the voice recognition. I have to say everything perfectly multiple times before the app recognizes my voice. I get penalized for speaking perfectly because this app doesn’t recognize my voice. That is unfair. I never had that issue with the free owl app. Anything that I spent hundreds of dollars on should work better than a free app. Every response to a negative review says that they are working to fix the voice recognition problem. Really? Why does that take a decade to fix? And they tell you to delete the app and reinstall it. The reason they do that is so that the App Store deletes your 1-star review. Their other advice is to use headphones with a microphone, even though smartphones no longer have a headphone port. The other thing that is annoying is that this app wants me to memorize long sentences exactly after hearing them once. And if I don’t say it fast enough, I get marked wrong. I can’t even finish a sentence! You can’t say something else that is equally correct. The stories are also annoying. I’ll be recording myself and in the middle of the story, it stops recording and every word says “We didn’t hear you say that.” Duh: I didn’t get to that part of the story yet. It also marks me wrong on words I say perfectly, especially short words. Then I listen back and I hear myself say the exact word perfectly. reviews.title: Real Authentic Review
reviews.text:
Tried it to learn Chinese from scratch. Would not recommend for beginners.
Lessons never explain what words or sentences mean. You just guess from pictures like you already know the language. That starts in the first lessons. No real teaching of basics.
Same method for other languages. I assume it’s fine if you already know some Chinese, but useless if you don’t, so I don’t see the point. 
Too expensive for an app that doesn’t actually teach.
Speech recognition also glitches. 
Again, Not for beginners. Skip it unless you already have the basics.
Also, all these positive reviews are obviously not authentic lol.

reviews.title: Poor voice recognition implementation renders app virtually useless with wireless headphones.
reviews.text: It is such a shame that the voice recognition flaws in this app haven’t been addressed. Voice recognition remains clunky and inconsistent with AirPods and other modern wireless headphones (By far the most popular earbuds for use with iOS devices) and it renders many lessons unable to be completed without disabling the microphone. The lessons are well constructed and informative otherwise but this fundamental bug remains a huge thorn in the side of the whole Rosetta Stone Experience. Come on Rosetta Stone, it’s not 2010 anymore, wireless headsets and earbuds are now the default, not the edge case, many devices no longer even support wired headsets and earbuds.

reviews.title: Immersion is the only way to really learn a language
reviews.text:
UPDATE: stopped working on my older iPad mini a couple days ago. I’ll restore 5 star rating if it gets fixed. I still believe in the Rosetta Stone approach but I’m very unhappy about the developer disallowing some of the older devices. 

UPDATE July 2026: older devices work again. Thank you! Back to 5 stars!

UPDATE July 30 2026: it stopped working. Very frustrating!

-——————————— 
If you rely on translating, I don’t think you can ever become fluent. Each language has words and phrases that simply cannot be translated. When you have a conversation in a foreign language and you have to translate the foreign words you hear into your native language and then translate your response from native back into foreign language, you will not only get tired and stressed out but your conversation will not be fluent and natural. What works for me are images. When learning the foreign word for flowers for example, I don’t translate into my native language but imagine a picture of flowers in my head. Then coming up with Blumen, fleures, flores, etc. in a foreign language conversation is much faster and requires much less brain power than translating. Those are just my 2 cents. This approach works best for me. I’m a foreign language major with 4 foreign languages. English is my 3rd language.  Everyone is different and has their preferred way of learning but I encourage everyone to try the immersion approach for one or two weeks and see how it goes.

reviews.title: Very unhelpful and unclear
reviews.text: I'm learning German, and the speaking lessons are the most difficult because of the app's inability to recognize the actual words being spoken. For example, I was in a room of people speaking English while doing my German speaking lesson, and i paused speaking because it was too loud. The app heard the voices and thought that they were saying the words on the screen, so it accepted it. However, when I tried to speak clearly and carefully in German, it would say that I am doing it wrong. The app is also very faulty when it comes to audio, because sometimes it does not give the right audio to match the picture. This caused problems with moving forward because of me not being able to match the sentence to the correct picture. Some audio cuts off at the beginning or the end, which makes it difficult to understand which picture it matches with. Also, finding out the direct translation is difficult because of the lack of explanation for each new word, and the only clue being a very vague picture with many things going on. This app is incredibly nit-picky, and I would recommend not downloading it and wasting lots of money.

reviews.title: Slow and glitchy
reviews.text:
Since the last update this app has become almost unusable for me. The audio either doesn’t play or is delayed and interrupted. It’s almost impossible to get through a lesson now - I can’t see how I can continue using this app. 
I generally enjoyed the lessons and learning style, though it can get a bit repetitive and it would be good to include additional  context and notes - TPI can only get so far associating pictures with words and after a while it becomes a memory exercise rather than understanding grammar and syntax (you’ll pick up on the main key words that allow you to guess the answer but not really understand the purpose of all the conjunctives). 
Even prior to this update, there were always two other point of frustration:
1. Each lesson takes an eternity to load - even when I’ve made it available offline.  This is really off-puting when you do a 5min lesson and then have to wait another 5mins for the next one to load. 
2. The voice recognition is really poor - you may as well just skip those lessons because you’re not going to get anything out of it - but if it’s a mixed lesson with speaking parts be prepared to be frustrated as you fail to progress beyond that exercise no matter how many times you say the word correctly. 
Tech is so good nowadays but it does not seem like Rosetta Stone can be bothered to invest in it.

reviews.title: Poorly implemented
reviews.text:
The very poor speech recognition is hard to forgive. It fails to even recognise single syllables. I have tried using the microphone on the phone, on my AirPods and on AirPod Pros, and it fails to hear me and complains about audio quality. Duolingo never had this issue. It removes any pleasure from the learning experience. Oh, and it needs to be in a quiet area to work so there is no chance of having a quick lesson on your daily commute.
When contacting support they will tell you to check the settings in the app but I have since discovered that this is a well known and long standing issue.

The other main issue are the poor quality stock images used. They are too small and frankly it isn’t always clear what is being shown, meaning it is a test of eyesight rather than language.

Other issues are images and text that occasionally are partially offscreen.

Update 20/01/2026
The audio issues persist. The app fails to hear anything one minute then complains that the sound is too loud the next. It seems especially bad when asking for single syllables yet bizarrely recognising full words composed of the same syllables.

I can’t tell if the app uses the AirPods microphones or not.

reviews.title: Poor audio recognition
reviews.text:
I have been using it everyday to learn Japanese over the past month. A couple of thoughts: 1. The app is easy to use leveraging pictures and repetition. This helps me to use it daily. 2. I learnt a bit Japanese during college so relatively easier for me to kickoff. I imagine the way it’s designed it will be hard for people who don’t have the basics. The app doesn’t cover basics. 3. The audio recognition is horrible. I will be yelling to the phone and the app still cannot be recognize my voice. It’s very weird that during same lesson sometimes it recognizes voice and sometimes it doesn’t. It’s not even the pronunciation but it just doesn’t catch my voice. I asked for support but the method they provided doesn’t solve the problem   Additionally, sometimes I knew I didn’t pronounce right but it would give me a perfect score. 4. I had my phone connected to my AirPod max and AirPod pro. Despite I am using my speaker or my AirPod pro the app will only connect to AirPod max (even it’s not close to my phone ). I have to disconnect my AirPod max Bluetooth first every time before I can  it. 
I unfortunately paid for the whole app not subscription. If I didn’t I would not have kept using the app because of the poor voice recognition.

reviews.title: Abysmal design and voice recognition
reviews.text: Its like they took an already dated windows app and shoehorned it into a mobile app. Speech recognition doesn’t work. The UI is garbage. Navigation is terrible. The point of apps like this is learning on the go, but this is so heavily built around speech recognition as to render any benefits of the mobile form factor worthless, unless I’m underestimating the market for massochists who want to be standing at a train station speaking random foreign language words into an app that couldn’t hear a harrier jump jet in a sound isolation booth let alone the word you are trying to get it to hear you speak. Also the ability to check dictionary to see what a word is just randomly appears and disappears as it pleases with no rhyme nor reason.
